how: Quick urine tests, in a lab or on the spot, look only for what they're built to find. In the US, most cover amphetamines, cocaine, cannabis, opiates and PCP, often benzos too. Cannabis tests don't catch synthetic cannabinoids, and tests for 'bath salts' haven't worked well.

Most opiate tests are set up for morphine. Fentanyl, methadone and buprenorphine don't react with them, and oxycodone only weakly. These need tests of their own, and some labs don't run them unless asked.
Most benzo tests can miss lorazepam and alprazolam (Xanax) unless the lab first treats the urine with an enzyme. Most labs don't. Clonazepam reacts poorly with the tests.

A negative only means the level was under the test's cutoff, or the test doesn't react to that drug. Lab tests like mass spectrometry find more. But they cost more and are mostly used to check positives. Many hospital labs can do little or none of it.
